nextGame.blurb: No. 1 Ohio State heads to Austin as a 2.5-point underdog against No. 4 Texas, with a total of just 50.5 pointing to a defensive slog. Two of the sport's heavyweights meet in Week 2 with real playoff seeding leverage on the line for the winner.

Oklahoma State stunned No. 6 Oregon 39-31 in Stillwater, ending a 21-game losing streak against FBS opponents and sending fans over the wall and the goal post into Theta Pond. Drew Mestemaker threw for 317 yards and two scores and ran for 109 more and a touchdown, more than enough to offset Devon Jackson's 96-yard pick-six for the 23.5-point favorite Ducks.

No. 2 Georgia hung 49 first-half points — matching the most productive half in school history — on the way to a 70-20 win over Western Kentucky. Gunner Stockton tied the school record with five touchdown passes to five different receivers in barely more than a quarter of work, and Tyriq Green added a 91-yard kickoff return score and an end-zone fumble recovery.

No. 3 Notre Dame took 14 seconds to score, as Adon Shuler's hit jarred the ball loose and Boubacar Traore returned it 24 yards, and the rout was on in a 52-0 win over Rice. C.J. Carr went 16 of 20 for 253 yards and four touchdowns before giving way in the third quarter, and the Irish forced four Owls turnovers while outgaining them 478-128.

No. 1 Ohio State heads to Austin as a 2.5-point underdog against No. 4 Texas, with a total of just 50.5 pointing to a defensive slog. Two of the sport's heavyweights meet in Week 2 with real playoff seeding leverage on the line for the winner.

No. 5 Indiana shut out Howard 55-0 in a shortened game, with Josh Hoover throwing four touchdown passes — three to Charlie Becker — before sitting at halftime. The Hoosiers rushed for 301 yards, added Rolijah Hardy's 19-yard pick-six, and pushed the FBS's longest active winning streak to 18.
Final: Florida A&M 7, #7 Miami 77.

No. 10 Texas A&M's defense took over late, scoring twice in the fourth quarter to blow open a 48-20 win over Arizona State. Marcel Reed threw three touchdown passes, and after Marco Jones rumbled 55 yards with a strip-sack fumble, Julio Humphrey added a 45-yard pick-six as the Aggies forced three Sun Devil turnovers.

No. 9 Ole Miss handled Charlotte 41-9, building the lead behind two Kewan Lacy touchdown runs and a pair of Trinidad Chambliss scoring passes. Lucas Carneiro chipped in from 57 and 41 yards as the 49ers managed only three field goals.

Michigan handed No. 11 Oklahoma a 17-10 loss in Ann Arbor, with Jordan Marshall's 1-yard plunge midway through the fourth — set up by one of two Sooners turnovers — providing the winning margin. Bryce Underwood ran for 87 yards including a 38-yard first-quarter touchdown and threw for 111 without a giveaway, and Oklahoma, favored by 5.5, never held the lead.

No. 8 LSU cruised past Louisiana Tech 45-14 behind a four-touchdown day from Sam Leavitt, who ran for three scores and threw for another. The Bulldogs' lone early answer was Jo. McRae's 100-yard interception return, one of three LSU giveaways on an otherwise comfortable night.
No. 13 Texas Tech travels to Oregon State as a 25.5-point favorite with a total of 52.5. The Red Raiders are carrying the Big 12's top playoff position right now, so style points on the road matter.

No. 12 Alabama trailed Kentucky 17-13 at the break and then didn't allow another point, blitzing the Wildcats 32-0 after halftime in a 45-17 win. Keelon Russell shook off two first-half picks to throw for 188 yards and a touchdown, Daniel Hill ran for 104 and a score, and Luke Metz's 34-yard interception return kept the Tide close early in a game that saw three turnovers by each side.

bubbleNote.blurb: Alabama sits at the 13 seed after moving up a spot, now just one place outside the field — the closest of the four bubble teams to crashing the bracket.

nextGame.blurb: No. 14 USC closes out the night as a 30.5-point favorite against Louisiana with the total at 58.5. A tune-up on paper, but the Trojans are sitting on the playoff bubble and can't afford a scare.

bubbleNote.blurb: USC holds steady at the 14 seed, two spots from the field, with no movement this week to show for it.

No. 18 Tennessee covered comfortably in a 45-24 win at Georgia Tech, with D. Lane's 41-yard pick-six one of two takeaways that flipped the game in the second quarter. Dylan Bishop ran for scores of 17 and 29 yards and D. Morris added a 47-yard touchdown run late to finish off the Yellow Jackets.
No. 20 Utah hosts Arkansas as a 12.5-point favorite in a late kickoff with the total set at 55.5. A double-digit hold at home would keep the Utes firmly in the Big 12 mix.

No. 21 Iowa survived Iowa State 16-16... make that 16-13, riding three Cade Buhr field goals — including two in the fourth quarter — to a rivalry win. The Hawkeyes were 14-point favorites but needed every kick after Iowa State's Konrardy answered with a 51-yarder in the third.

No. 22 Houston piled up 591 yards and buried Southern 77-6 in a game briefly played without stadium lights after a power outage. Conner Weigman threw three touchdown passes in a game and a half before handing off to Keisean Henderson, who added two more scores through the air and a 54-yard touchdown run as 10 different Cougars carried the ball for 388 rushing yards.

No. 24 Louisville got into the win column with a 59-13 rout of Villanova, piling up 635 yards of offense. Lincoln Kienholz threw for 332 yards and two touchdowns — including a 69-yarder to Jaleel Skinner and a 61-yard strike to Lawayne McCoy — and ran for two more before exiting after three quarters.

No. 23 Missouri turned a halftime tie into a 38-21 Border War win in Lawrence after Robert Woodyard Jr. forced back-to-back takeaways early in the second half and Austin Simmons turned both into touchdowns. Jamal Roberts ran for 125 yards and a 64-yard score, and Kansas finished with three turnovers in a game the Tigers were favored to win by four.

No. 25 Virginia put the game away in the opening quarter, as Beau Pribula threw three touchdown passes before the first break in a 59-3 win over Norfolk State. The Cavaliers threw for six scores in all, and reserve linebacker Justin Rowe capped it with a 50-yard interception return as Virginia forced three turnovers.
Final: Florida A&M 7, #7 Miami 77.

fieldStorylines.blurb: Ohio State and Texas are both currently sitting in the playoff bye band, and one of them is leaving Austin with a loss. The winner locks in first-round-bye positioning; the loser drops back into the scrum.
Georgia holds the SEC's automatic bid at No. 2 with Texas just two spots back at No. 4 — the tightest of margins with the Longhorns hosting Ohio State.
Texas Tech leads the Big 12 race at No. 13 with BYU right on its heels at No. 15, a two-spot gap that leaves the league's auto bid very much unsettled.
Ohio State sits atop the Big Ten at No. 1 with Indiana four spots back at No. 5 — the most comfortable of the three major-conference leads, but hardly a runaway.
